classification.difficultyReason: Requires identifying a right triangle outside a rotated square, finding its shorter side and using perpendicular equal sides to determine the remaining height.

content.prompt: A square box of side 7 cm is leaning against a vertical wall, as shown below. Find the height of point $C$ above the floor.

spec.description: Unshaded tilted square ABCD resting at A on a horizontal floor and touching a vertical wall at D. AB and BC each retain the printed 7 cm label; the angle at B is marked right. The floor distance from A to the wall is labelled 5 cm. Ordinary source blue linework is rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC=CD=DA=7 cm; adjacent square sides are perpendicular. With A=(0,0), D=(5,sqrt(24)), B=(-sqrt(24),5) and C=(5-sqrt(24),5+sqrt(24)), all square relationships and the given floor distance hold exactly. Coordinates are construction data, not additional printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and labels appear; no calculated lengths or heights are shown.

answer.short:
$(5+2\sqrt6)\text{ cm}$

Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the height of $D$, then add the vertical rise from $D$ to $C$.
answer.worked:
Let $E$ be the point where the wall meets the floor. Then $AE=5$ cm and $AD=7$ cm. In right-angled triangle $AED$,
$$\begin{align*}DE^2&=7^2-5^2\\DE^2&=24\\DE&=2\sqrt6\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Since $DC=AD$ and $DC$ is perpendicular to $AD$, rotating side $AD$ through a right angle interchanges its horizontal and vertical components. Thus the vertical rise from $D$ to $C$ equals $AE=5$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Height of }C&=DE+5\\\text{Height of }C&=(2\sqrt6+5)\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
